adds.title: Transgender rights in Texas (Wikipedia)
adds.summary: Wikipedia state-rights article (accessed 4 Oct 2026): Governor Abbott signed the Women's Privacy Act on 22 September 2025; it requires bathrooms matching the sex on one's birth certificate and explicitly applies to public schools, universities, prisons and Texas government buildings, with $25,000 (first) / $125,000 (subsequent) facility fines, effective 4 December 2025. Documents that Texas' most recent gender-placements statute reaches prisons — but on restroom use, not on cell/facility assignment or trans-prisoner housing placement.

adds.title: LGBTQ people in prison (Wikipedia) — Gibson v. Collier (2019) ruling
adds.summary: Wikipedia article on LGBTQ prisoners (accessed 4 Oct 2026), Gibson v. Collier section: Vanessa Lynn Gibson, a transgender woman incarcerated in Texas by the Texas Department of Criminal Justice and diagnosed with gender dysphoria, was denied gender-confirmation surgery because TDCJ's official treatment policy excluded GCS. The federal district court denied the state's immunity defences but ruled against her on the Eighth Amendment claim; the Fifth Circuit affirmed dismissal (no deliberate indifference; refusing GCS is a permissible medical choice under Kosilek), with Judge Barksdale dissenting on summary-judgement procedure.

records.note: Texas: no statute mandating birth-sex prison placement per se was found within budget; the operative placement-relevant law found is the Women's Privacy Act (signed 22 Sep 2025, in force 4 Dec 2025) which extends birth-certificate-sex restroom rules to prisons. Documented ruling: Gibson v. Collier (5th Cir. 2019) — TDCJ's official treatment policy excludes gender-confirmation surgery, a denial the courts upheld, with a procedural dissent; the case shows TDCJ carries a formal anti-trans care policy but says nothing about male/female facility assignment. No Texas-specific special-unit, solitary/segregation practice, or trans-prisoner housing case was documented in the fetched sources; none fabricated.

adds.title: Transgender rights in Tennessee (Wikipedia) — Prison section
adds.summary: Wikipedia state-rights article, Prison section (accessed 4 Oct 2026): in April 2024 the Tennessee State Legislature passed a bill banning gender-affirming care for Tennessee inmates; and under the 2026 'Riley Gaines Women's Safety and Protection Act' transgender inmates are to be placed in prisons based on their sex assigned at birth (birth-sex placement mandate). The same 2026 Act also bans trans women from women's shelters (adjacent provision).

records.note: Tennessee: birth-sex placement is now statutory. Per the Wikipedia state-rights article: April 2024 law bans gender-affirming care for state inmates; the 2026 Riley Gaines Women's Safety and Protection Act mandates that transgender inmates be placed in prisons based on sex assigned at birth (signed pathway reported as passed April 2026 alongside shelter/bathroom provisions). Practical import: a trans woman detained in Tennessee is placed in a men's facility by law, with no gender-affirming care. No Tennessee-specific special-unit, solitary/segregation practice, or documented trans-prisoner housing case/ruling was found within budget (search + 1 fetch used); none fabricated.
